> **Delivery baseline — 2026-11-10:** Baseline workstream B. Reuse the existing projection and Cook behavior; ordinary trusted binding production remains a required missing connection. The first whole-use tracer does not remove the other specified supported allocation forms. See the [release scope and agent coordination](../canonical-ingredient-correction/proposal.md#dependable-portions-delivery-baseline--accepted-2026-11-10).

## Why

Ingredient-only scaling leaves step quantities contradictory. Step uses need explicit revision-bound associations to original recipe demand while cooking remains available when a mapping is uncertain.

## Outcome and Scope

Mandatory ingredient-use scaling, coherent ingredient/step projection and current-recipe reading at recorded prepared counts. No general formula language, prose-wide numeric replacement or new grocery demand. Explicit partial amounts remain original after total correction and still scale with portions; relative language stays relative, with original readable wording for inconsistent allocations. Cook mode omits the routine step-uncertainty notice and duplicate header ingredients link; phone Edit/View Original actions return to the right while the view toggle stays left and tablet controls retain their lower-left layout.

## Implementation baseline and remaining delivery

The projection engine, original-step editor, coherent refresh, prepared-count consumers and Cook cleanup already exist. Existing unit, PostgreSQL and browser owners exercise whole, absolute, fraction, remainder, fixed and per-item behavior; their recorded results remain tied to their tested candidates. They are reusable implementation, not an instruction to build another engine.

The missing connection is ordinary trusted relationship production and maintenance through import and saved edits. Current conversion creates empty bindings and projection fixtures seed them. Group 0 in tasks.md owns that missing producer/validator and its real workflow acceptance. Groups 1–3 retain acceptance of supported behavior and identify only demonstrated gaps; group 4 and task 5.3 retain outstanding integration/release qualification. This change is not complete until ordinary URL/photo and manual-correction flows reach supported scaling without seeded relationships. Bilingual catalogue adoption and Similar-search UI are deferred from this release. Other intake expansion follows in later increments and is outside the first selected increment, not silently removed from the eventual requirements.

## What Changes

- Automatically maintain ingredient-to-step relationships during import and after saved ingredient or step edits, using the ordinary editor without special markup or mandatory manual linking. Reuse deterministic revalidation; allow a workflow AI task to propose replacements when necessary, subject to server evidence validation and stale-write protection. Uncertain text remains original and readable.
- **BREAKING:** adopt the applicable shared [contract](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md) with explicit compatibility/failure behavior.
- Preserve user decisions and existing safety boundaries in the shared [review](../canonical-ingredient-correction/review.md).
- Complete and reconcile adversarial acceptance from the shared [corpus](../canonical-ingredient-correction/acceptance-corpus.md); this consolidation changes planning artifacts only.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `cooking`: project validated uses and preserve cooking context.
- `supper-servings`: include step uses in shared portions projection.
- `recipe-editing`: guard instruction edits in original basis.

## Impact

Depends on the canonical foundation and companion ownership map as specified in design.md. Future apply must synchronize OpenAPI, generated clients, consumers and stateful mocks where affected, and qualify actual persistence/workflow seams. Planning existence does not establish implementation readiness.
# Design

## Context and Existing Ownership

Current `CooksMode`, stepParser/instructionPresentation, RecipeService instruction PATCH and shared serving projection own reading/editing. `CookingStepProjection` already validates revision-bound spans and projects supported allocation forms; `IngredientProjectionService` supplies coherent ingredient/step context. `CanonicalRecipeContentStore` guards original edits and revalidates prior bindings. Reuse those owners, stable original sections/steps and the foundation's contentRevision; no separate step quantity store or replacement projection engine.

Ordinary binding production is still missing: conversion creates empty bindings and instruction Save retains only prior bindings. The existing `CanonicalIngredientEditPostgresTests` step/allocation partials and `LiveBrowser_Cooking*` fixtures exercise consumer behavior with seeded relationships. Their passing evidence cannot establish that an ordinary imported or edited recipe acquires trusted relationships. Group 0 supplies this missing connection; groups 1–3 reconcile and extend existing owners only where their acceptance is absent or affected.

## Decisions and Tradeoffs

Use [shared bindings](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md) for mention, whole, absolute, fraction, remainder, fixed and per-item roles. Spans are UTF-16 half-open with expected text and exact text/content revisions; Unicode boundaries and duplicate occurrences must be tested. Structured segments could avoid offsets but would force a richer editor/import rewrite; validated spans fit the existing ordinary text editor. An invalid span leaves its original text untouched, not guessed.

Check allocations only in explicit exhaustive same-row sequences. Alternative branches, mentions and reused references never add demand. A numeric remainder requires compatible known uses and correlation-safe arithmetic; intervals are not independent random allocations. One row's invalid sequence cannot invalidate other proven bindings. Fixed and per-item semantics need explicit evidence.

## First Observable Slice

### Accepted automatic reevaluation after import and edits — 2026-11-10

The ordinary recipe editor remains the user entry point. No special recipe syntax
or manual ingredient-to-step linking screen is required. Fresh intake and committed
ingredient/step changes use the same relationship validation rules. At Save,
revalidate unaffected proof and apply the already approved total/allocation rules;
invalidate affected unsafe relationships before any later projection can use them.
Unknown quantities and explicitly cleared rows/steps remain valid user decisions.

When deterministic revalidation cannot establish a supported relationship, an AI
task may propose relationships through the existing workflow system using captured
saved originals, stable IDs and content/text revisions. This is relationship
reevaluation, not a new source reimport or a replacement of human-authored facts.
Alex explicitly accepted this first-release boundary: AI reevaluation may maintain
scaling relationships but may not rewrite saved ingredient descriptions, amounts,
units or instruction wording. Recipe rewriting is outside this workflow's scope.
The server must establish the required association, numeric role and whole/partial
evidence independently of a provider's confidence or `validated` label. The bounded
evidence rules still require engineering design and adversarial acceptance; the
permission to use AI does not resolve that missing validator by assumption.

Reuse existing workflow scheduling, lifecycle, retry and publication owners. Scope
work to affected relationships; a no-op or unrelated metadata change does not
trigger an AI evaluation. Capture the committed input revision, deduplicate repeated
delivery for that revision, and reject late results if current facts no longer match.
Do not relink by row position or restore cleared facts. Provider failure or inability
to prove a relationship leaves saved edits intact and affected wording original;
unaffected validated relationships remain usable. Successful binding publication
advances the coherent content revision through the canonical owner, changes no

- **WHEN** an import's final content validation identifies missing ingredient or usable-step content and the retained recipe contains editable original content, with no existing report
- **THEN** a system flag enters the existing Ready for review queue with a short explanatory comment and no launched repair
- **AND** image, category, transport and other arbitrary failures do not create that flag; existing reports retain their reasons, comments, attribution and repair state

#### Scenario: Unchanged human-review flag remains manual
- **WHEN** a person saves the unchanged system flag with its unchanged explanatory comment
- **THEN** no repair is launched and the existing flag is retained unchanged

#### Scenario: A changed comment requests correction
- **WHEN** a person adds or changes a nonblank comment on eligible Ingredients or Steps feedback without Duplicate
- **THEN** the existing contextual correction rules apply, preserving their capture, repeated-feedback and stale-write safeguards


### Requirement: Display returned issue indicators

Detail and library surfaces that receive issue status SHALL display Reported for reported and Review for readyToReview, with accessible descriptions distinguishing a reported recipe from a recipe needing human review. Detail SHALL display returned re-import failure guidance. Indicator rendering SHALL NOT imply immediate refresh of every already loaded library surface.

#### Scenario: Render a returned report status
- **WHEN** detail or a supported library card receives reported status
- **THEN** it displays Reported with the accessible description Recipe reported

#### Scenario: Render a returned review status
- **WHEN** detail or a supported library card receives readyToReview status
- **THEN** it displays Review with the accessible description Recipe ready for review

#### Scenario: Review does not claim automatic completion
- **WHEN** an issue is readyToReview, whether raised by content validation or after contextual processing
- **THEN** review guidance says Ready for review and does not claim that re-import completed merely from that status


### Requirement: Offer explicit manual resolution for an existing issue

An existing issue's Review issue form SHALL offer Mark as resolved with an explanation that it removes the recipe from Needs review. A readyToReview issue SHALL give that action stronger visual emphasis and ask the person to check the recipe before resolving. A new report form SHALL omit resolution. Existing requirements govern opening and initializing the form, reason/note behavior and pending/failure guidance.

#### Scenario: Review a reported issue
- **WHEN** the Review issue form displays a reported issue
- **THEN** Mark as resolved and Removes this recipe from Needs review. are displayed

#### Scenario: Review an updated recipe
- **WHEN** the form displays a readyToReview issue
- **THEN** Mark as resolved has stronger emphasis and the form says to check the recipe and mark it resolved when it looks right

#### Scenario: No saved issue exists
- **WHEN** the new Report issue form is opened without a saved issue
- **THEN** Mark as resolved is absent

#### Scenario: Review without claiming a repair
- **WHEN** a system content flag is opened
- **THEN** the form explains that ingredients and steps need review and still offers a comment for eligible automatic correction
- **AND** Mark as resolved removes feedback without certifying content or changing readiness



### Requirement: Reuse active feedback and avoid unchanged terminal retries

Eligible contextual feedback matching a linked active attempt SHALL reuse its import ID. Changed feedback SHALL be rejected while that attempt is active. Matching feedback for a linked terminal attempt SHALL save without starting another attempt. Changed eligible feedback after a terminal attempt SHALL be considered for a new attempt rather than treated as the previous feedback.

#### Scenario: Repeat active feedback
- **WHEN** eligible contextual feedback has normalized reasons and trimmed note matching the linked pending or processing attempt
- **THEN** the response returns that same import ID with reimportStarted true without creating another attempt

#### Scenario: Change active feedback
- **WHEN** feedback changes while its linked attempt is pending or processing
- **THEN** submission returns 409 without replacing saved feedback

#### Scenario: Repeat terminal feedback
- **WHEN** normalized feedback matches the linked completed, failed or paused attempt
- **THEN** submission saves without starting another attempt or returning a new import ID

#### Scenario: Change terminal feedback
- **WHEN** feedback changes after the linked attempt is terminal and the new feedback is eligible
- **THEN** it is considered for a new contextual attempt, subject to launch success

Unchanged saved feedback without a retained original repair command SHALL be a no-op rather than inventing a new command from today's recipe. Existing captured-command retries/reconciliation and attributed active attempts SHALL retain their original behavior.

#### Scenario: Save an unchanged explanatory system comment
- **WHEN** a person saves the same reasons and explanatory comment on a system-created review flag without a retained repair command
- **THEN** its comment and report history remain unchanged and no automatic correction is launched

#### Scenario: Retry a retained original command
- **WHEN** unchanged feedback has an existing retained repair command whose acceptance needs reconciliation
- **THEN** existing retry/unknown-outcome rules use that command rather than a fresh capture
# Spec Delta

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Generate privacy-scrubbed portable export bundle

Authorized GET /api/recipes/{id}/share with household access and member context SHALL return portable version 1.0 with source wfs-share. It SHALL preserve core text, structured instructions and up to five original images, deriving ingredient strings from current canonical text. Ratings/notes SHALL be null; internal entity IDs and attribution SHALL be omitted. This text-only share SHALL NOT claim full-fidelity quantity, basis or evidence preservation.

#### Scenario: Scrub personal notes and rating
- **WHEN** an authorized export request succeeds for a recipe containing household notes and a rating
- **THEN** the returned bundle sets both `notes` and `rating` to null in the exported recipe payload

#### Scenario: Preserve structured instructions and original images up to five
- **WHEN** an authorized export request succeeds for a recipe with structured instructions and multiple original images
- **THEN** the bundle preserves the HowToSections and steps, and includes up to five original images with MIME types and base64 payloads

#### Scenario: Wrap flat instruction strings in a default section
- **WHEN** an authorized export request succeeds for a recipe whose raw metadata stores flat instruction strings
- **THEN** the bundle wraps the steps inside a default section named Instructions

#### Scenario: Reject export when recipe lacks hero image
- **WHEN** an authorized export request is made for a recipe without a hero image in storage
- **THEN** the API returns 400 Bad Request indicating the recipe must have a hero image before it can be shared

#### Scenario: Reject export when member context header is missing
- **WHEN** a request is made to GET `/api/recipes/{id}/share` without member context
- **THEN** the API returns 400 Bad Request requiring member context

#### Scenario: Reject export when recipe is not found
- **WHEN** an authorized export request is made for a recipe identifier that does not exist
- **THEN** the API returns 404 Not Found

#### Scenario: Export current canonical text without private repair state
- **WHEN** a canonical recipe with accepted corrections and retained private source or human-protection evidence is shared
- **THEN** version 1.0 contains the saved canonical ingredient strings in order without private repair state or local ingredient identities
- **AND** the portable share is not represented as a current-format backup or a full-fidelity quantity transfer

### Requirement: Accept and persist imported recipe bundle into library

Import recipe SHALL POST the bundle to /api/recipes/import-bundle. The API SHALL validate version 1.0, source wfs-share, required content, at most five originals and base64 payloads; assign a new recipe ID on collision; persist readiness and importing member attribution; save media and return 201. Ingredient strings SHALL initialize canonical lines with new local identities, without inventing missing structured quantity or serving-basis evidence.

#### Scenario: Accept valid bundle and persist ready recipe with importing member attribution
- **WHEN** an authorized import request with a valid bundle payload succeeds
- **THEN** the API persists a new ready recipe entity attributed to the requesting family member, saves hero and original images, and returns 201 Created with the created recipe DTO

#### Scenario: Reassign recipe identifier when bundle identifier collides with existing entity
- **WHEN** the bundle's recipe identifier already exists in the database
- **THEN** the API generates a new unique identifier for the imported recipe and persists it without overwriting the existing entity

#### Scenario: Restore optional notes and rating into newly persisted entity
- **WHEN** a valid bundle contains notes and a rating
- **THEN** the newly created recipe entity persists those notes and rating values in the database and metadata store

#### Scenario: Reject bundle with unsupported version
- **WHEN** an import request supplies a version string other than 1.0
- **THEN** the API returns 400 Bad Request indicating the bundle version is unsupported

#### Scenario: Reject bundle with malformed payload or invalid image base64
- **WHEN** an import request supplies empty ingredients, empty instructions, more than five original images, or non-base64 image strings
- **THEN** the API returns 400 Bad Request with an error message describing the violation

#### Scenario: Import text without structured quantities
- **WHEN** a valid version-1.0 share contains ingredient strings but no trustworthy structured quantity or basis facts
- **THEN** import preserves their exact text and order using new local line identities and represents missing facts as unknown
- **AND** it does not parse text into asserted amounts, inherit exporting-household human protection or claim verified source evidence

#### Scenario: Legitimate unquantified imported content
- **WHEN** imported text includes an ingredient without a numeric amount
- **THEN** that missing number alone does not flag the recipe for correction or prevent its existing ready import behavior
# Spec Delta

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Clean failed-capture residue subject to the current recipe guard

For a failed-capture residue command, maintenance SHALL retain a recipe that is discoverable, has a nonblank name with images or synthesis, or retains persisted ingredient, instruction or canonical content (including explicit saved empty values). Otherwise, when the recipe exists, it SHALL delete its retained directory and remove the database recipe, recording the outcome.

#### Scenario: Safe residue
- **WHEN** the command targets a non-ready-shaped undiscoverable placeholder without persisted recipe content and successful persistence is possible
- **THEN** its directory and recipe are removed and the command completes

#### Scenario: Recipe became ready-shaped
- **WHEN** the target recipe has a nonblank name and positive image count
- **THEN** the recipe is retained and the command is skipped

#### Scenario: Missing recipe
- **WHEN** the target recipe no longer exists
- **THEN** the command completes with recipe-not-found

#### Scenario: Preserve accepted content corrections
- **WHEN** deferred cleanup encounters a recipe with persisted original content, including human-cleared ingredient or instruction collections
- **THEN** it retains the recipe, its files and reports instead of deleting accepted corrections
## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Share one authoritative projection across consumers

Home dated ingredients, proposed/assigned detail, cooking and groceries SHALL share canonical original facts and server-owned dated scaling. Temporary previews use that owner with an independent count. Assigned reads reject stale occurrence identity; original reads remain compatible through the common adapter. Reads SHALL NOT assign, save portions, call providers or materialize preparation.

#### Scenario: Plan and cook for six
- **WHEN** a recipe with basis two and 200 g pasta is planned for six
- **THEN** dated detail and cooking show 600 g and its grocery contribution is 600 g

#### Scenario: Proposed date before assignment
- **WHEN** an unassigned candidate is read for a date configured for four
- **THEN** its default dated projection uses four without requiring assignment or changing saved state

#### Scenario: No selected or proposed date
- **WHEN** recipe reading has no date context
- **THEN** its default is original quantities and an explicitly selected 2/4/6 preview remains a separate read-only projection

#### Scenario: Converted and edited canonical record
- **WHEN** a canonical content revision replaces legacy live supply reads
- **THEN** all quantity consumers use that revision and its original amounts, with grocery normalization/aggregation after projection rather than another recipe ingredient parser

#### Scenario: Home ingredients and dated Cook agree
- **WHEN** Home Tonight and Cook refer to the same captured assigned recipe, date and effective portions
- **THEN** Home uses the shared dated projection with the same reliable amounts and completeness before display rounding, including frozen prepared portions
- **AND** late results from an earlier recipe/date/occurrence cannot replace the current list; pending, failure or changed-plan state is explicit rather than labeling original strings as scaled
- **AND** opening the ingredient list performs no assignment, portions, grocery, preparation or completion write

### Requirement: Scale independently aligned ingredient amounts

Known canonical amounts SHALL scale only for their stable original-basis line identities. Missing/uncertain lines do not invalidate other known lines. Legacy name/source matching is a conservative conversion/import boundary, not a second live quantity owner. Unknown/conflicting facts retain text. Reads SHALL NOT guess text numbers, call AI or repair saved data.

#### Scenario: Four-portion shells recipe with omitted seasonings
- **WHEN** original yield is four and canonical lines converted from coherent unambiguous source facts retain 12 shells, 1 onion, 450 g beef and 500 ml marinara while salt and pepper lack reliable amounts
- **THEN** preview two shows 6 shells, 0.5 onion, 225 g beef and 250 ml marinara; preview four shows 12, 1, 450 g and 500 ml; preview six shows 18, 1.5, 675 g and 750 ml
- **AND** seasonings retain their original text and honest completeness state, other verified lines scale, and the recipe is not described as completely quantified

#### Scenario: Missing middle ingredient
- **WHEN** a lime line has no structured amount between verified garlic and honey, followed by known salmon and sesame amounts
- **THEN** garlic, honey, salmon and sesame retain their own amounts and scale independently; lime is not given honey's quantity

#### Scenario: Ambiguous duplicate or changed source
- **WHEN** legacy conversion cannot associate an amount unambiguously, source/current strings conflict or an association has become invalid without an explicit accepted correction
- **THEN** affected amounts are unresolved instead of guessed, and unrelated verified bindings remain usable

#### Scenario: Intentional unquantified text and packages
- **WHEN** an ingredient says salt to taste or oil for frying, or a verified quantity is two 400 g cans
- **THEN** the direction remains ordinary unquantified text and scaling changes the can count without multiplying its package size or instruction numbers

#### Scenario: Shared consumers and unknown basis
- **WHEN** the same aligned recipe/count is read through preview, proposed or assigned detail, cooking and grocery contribution
- **THEN** reliable numeric amounts and completeness agree across consumers before display rounding
- **AND** an unknown original yield prevents a scaling factor, offers original evidence/correction, and is never replaced by family size

#### Scenario: Explicit canonical identities distinguish duplicate names
- **WHEN** distinct canonical lines have the same descriptive name but their own accepted amounts and stable identities
- **THEN** scaling retains each association without re-matching names or inventing identity from grocery grouping keys

#### Scenario: Valid unquantified lines and correction flags
- **WHEN** a canonical collection includes legitimate unquantified directions beside numeric amounts
- **THEN** the directions remain ordinary text without a correction flag solely for missing numbers; technical completeness and saved household report membership retain their separate meanings

# Network topology reference

Load only for network/deployment, cookie or SSE origin work. These are source-verified
implementation facts, not proof of a running deployment.

## Browser and server URLs are different

[config.ts](../../pwa/src/lib/constants/config.ts) and the
[Kiota adapter](../../pwa/src/lib/api/api-client.ts) default the browser API base to
an empty string. [useScheduleStream](../../pwa/src/hooks/useScheduleStream.ts) builds
`/api/stream` when that base is empty and uses credentials. Same-origin browser
requests behind Traefik retain `/api`; do not expose Docker service names to browsers.
Do not require a literal `/` base: callers concatenate paths, and a leading `/` base
can produce `//api/...`. Inspect each affected URL builder when changing the base.

[serverFetch](../../pwa/src/lib/api/server-client.ts) concatenates `API_INTERNAL_URL`
and the endpoint without normalization. Its default and the production override use
`http://api:9001`, the configured absolute container-network URL. It explicitly forwards
`h_access` in the Cookie header and identity as `X-Family-Member-Id`. This internal
request does not change the browser origin. The retired claim that both bases must
be `/`, or that internal absolute URLs inherently break SSR cookies, was incorrect.

## Configuration owners

- [apps.yml](../../docker/compose/apps.yml) defines API `/api` routing, the dedicated
  priority-100 stream router and `sse-headers@file` middleware. The prefix is retained.
  [traefik_dynamic.yml](../../docker/compose/traefik_dynamic.yml) defines the headers
  and additional local-host routes; inspect the composed configuration for deployment.
- [production-overrides.yml](../../docker/compose/production-overrides.yml) binds the
  host `DATA_ROOT` location to `/data`; the base API sets container `DATA_ROOT=/data`.
  [production.yml](../../docker/compose/production.yml) separately overrides container
  `DATA_ROOT` with the host variable. Do not assume those different compositions
  produce the same storage path. Verify rendered env and mounts before deployment.
- Both production files default Traefik host ports to 9100 (HTTP) and 9180 (admin),
  with overrides. These are legacy configuration facts, not public-release requirements.
  Current public installation and qualification guidance lives in
  [release-template/synology/README.md](../../release-template/synology/README.md).
- `DOMAIN_NAME` is a host routing value, not a URL with scheme/path.
  [auth.ts](../../pwa/src/lib/auth.ts) and
  [identity cookies](../../pwa/src/lib/identity/cookie.ts) read optional
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_COOKIE_DOMAIN`. A parent domain is not universally required.

Verify the selected Compose combination and server/client behavior rather than
copying historical environment claims. Static source inspection does not establish
SSE delivery, cookie behavior in a deployed browser, or persistent-volume recovery.
Existing owners are RecipeService, SupperIngredientProjection, import/synthesis/publication, generated clients, editor, stateful mocks and PostgreSQL persistence. Reuse implemented behavior; future code work follows the selected owner tasks. Shared shapes live in [contracts.md](contracts.md); [review](review.md) and the [acceptance corpus](acceptance-corpus.md) distinguish this release from deferred bilingual work. Companions: [groceries](../restore-dependable-grocery-interactions/proposal.md), [bilingual identity](../bilingual-shopping-identity/proposal.md), [steps](../scale-cooking-step-ingredients/proposal.md), [migration/recovery](../migrate-canonical-recipe-model/proposal.md).


Fresh URL/photo qualification, retained review-material repair, ordinary original
editing, clear protection and report semantics are documented in [design](design.md)
and their capability deltas. [Tasks](tasks.md) maps those implemented foundations
to remaining work and evidence; no completed slice must be rebuilt solely because
its containing aggregate task is unchecked.

## Coordinated absolute-use slice 2

The accepted whole-use deployment remains the prerequisite. The next selected slice
adds ordinary explicit absolute-use production through existing URL/photo and guarded
Save hooks: total 200→250 preserves explicit 50, six portions from basis four displays
75 in Cook and one 375 grocery demand. Step edits replace proof; ambiguous associations
abstain quietly. Existing whole and allocation roles remain preservation requirements.

Selected tasks, sole-writer ownership, dependencies, scenario mapping, evidence and
unchanged lifecycle dispositions are recorded in
[tasks](tasks.md#coordinated-absolute-use-slice-2). Commit, push and exact-commit DV
deployment are explicitly authorized for this one completed slice. Stop after accepted
DV integration into recipe-view-redesign and provide the next prompt without launching
it. Unfinished aggregates remain open; no archival or main-spec promotion follows.

# Next.js QA

Follow [contract/testing](../../core/contract-testing.md) and the selected scope.

# Locators and E2E Test Stability

Use stable interaction locators and inspect DOM, data and state evidence when diagnosing failures.

## The Locator Hierarchy
1.  **MANDATORY:** `page.getByTestId('...')` - Use this for almost everything interactive.
2.  **ACCEPTABLE:** `page.getByRole('...', { name: '...' })` - Use this for core accessibility assertions (e.g., confirming the Main Menu is labeled correctly).
3.  **FORBIDDEN:** `page.locator('css=.some-class > div:nth-child(2)')` - Do not use generated CSS classes or complex DOM paths.

## Anti-Pattern: Flaky Locators
*   **Wrong:** `await page.click('button.submit-btn')`
*   **Why it's bad:** If the design changes and the class is renamed to `primary-btn`, the test breaks even though the functionality works. 
*   **Right:** `await page.getByTestId('submit-btn').click()`

## Diagnosing "Element Not Found" Errors
If Playwright reports that an element could not be found:
1.  **Check the Test ID:** Did the developer forget to add the `data-testid` to the React component?
2.  **Check the Data:** Is the mock API returning the right data? If the mock returns an empty list, the element won't render.
3.  **Check the State:** Did a previous action fail to complete? (e.g., the test clicked "Save", but the API returned a 400, so the next screen never loaded).
"}

You can use it to write **End-to-End (E2E)** testing. This guide will show you how to set up Playwright with Next.js and write your first tests. ## Quickstart The fastest way to get started is to use `create-next-app` with the [with-playwright example](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-playwright). This will create a Next.js project complete with Playwright configured. ```bash package="pnpm" pnpm create next-app --example with-playwright with-playwright-app ``` ```bash package="npm" npx create-next-app@latest --example with-playwright with-playwright-app ``` ```bash package="yarn" yarn create next-app --example with-playwright with-playwright-app ``` ```bash package="bun" bun create next-app --example with-playwright with-playwright-app ``` ## Manual setup To install Playwright, run the following command: ```bash package="pnpm" pnpm create playwright ``` ```bash package="npm" npm init playwright ``` ```bash package="yarn" yarn create playwright ``` ```bash package="bun" bun create playwright ``` This will take you through a series of prompts to set up and configure Playwright for your project, including adding a `playwright.config.ts` file. Please refer to the [Playwright installation guide](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro#installation) for the step-by-step guide. ## Creating your first Playwright E2E test Create two new Next.js pages: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" import Link from 'next/link' export default function Page() { return (

Home

About
) } ``` ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" import Link from 'next/link' export default function Page() { return (

About

Home
) } ``` ```tsx filename="pages/index.ts" import Link from 'next/link' export default function Home() { return (

Home

About
) } ``` ```tsx filename="pages/about.ts" import Link from 'next/link' export default function About() { return (

About

Home
) } ``` Then, add a test to verify that your navigation is working correctly: ```ts filename="tests/example.spec.ts" import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test' test('should navigate to the about page', async ({ page }) => { // Start from the index page (the baseURL is set via the webServer in the playwright.config.ts) await page.goto('http://localhost:3000/') // Find an element with the text 'About' and click on it await page.click('text=About') // The new URL should be "/about" (baseURL is used there) await expect(page).toHaveURL('http://localhost:3000/about') // The new page should contain an h1 with "About" await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('About') }) ``` > **Good to know**: You can use `page.goto("/")` instead of `page.goto("http://localhost:3000/")`, if you add [`"baseURL": "http://localhost:3000"`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testoptions#test-options-base-url) to the `playwright.config.ts` [configuration file](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-configuration). ### Testing instant navigations If you're using Cache Components, the `instant()` helper from `@next/playwright` lets you assert what is visible immediately after a navigation, before any dynamic content streams in. See the [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) and the [`instant` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) for setup and examples. ### Running your Playwright tests Playwright will simulate a user navigating your application using three browsers: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, this requires your Next.js server to be running. We recommend running your tests against your production code to more closely resemble how your application will behave.
